description: A probable or confident person_evidence link to a person with a recorded namesake (namesakes[]) stands only when something in its source ties it to that person: (a) another party of the same source linked at probable or better to the person's spouse, parent or child, who has a given name and was not made from that source alone; or (b) an occupation or street address of the person's party on that source equal to the same field on another source's link to the person. A link whose assertion is absent basis is never judged. Replayed statically by the research_append precondition (namesakeTieInvariants), with every probable or confident link to the person as a possible voucher; a write is judged by namesakeCallCheck, which counts only links standing before the call.
format: expect: fire | silent, judged for the person_evidence entry named by `write` in `research` (the document as it stands after the write). `tree` holds the tree. The tree's people are FamilySearch-shaped ids, since the replay passes no starting tree. A case with `known_let_through: true` is silent although the link is the namesake's: a let-through the guard accepts, labelled so it is never read as a correct allow.

cases.why: A voter register naming only the principal: nothing on it ties the link to P rather than to his namesake (the Gaetjen register shape).
The other party of a marriage is linked to someone who is not P's spouse, parent or child (georg-gajdosch call 76).
The bride is linked to P's wife, but that wife was created from this marriage alone, so she cannot vouch for it.
The wife's persona on the census is linked to P's wife only at speculative.
Both records give the residence as a village name, with no street address: every family in the village shares it (georg 'Lidečko').
The residence value both records carry is the census date, not a place.
The census head is linked to P and the wife to P's wife (joseph-david XSMQ-X77 shape).
P is the son on his father's census; the head is linked to P's father (the Flynn household of ut_person_evidence_013).
A baptism: the child persona's father assertion is linked to both P and the son, the father's name to P, the child's name to the son.
A death record whose father appears only in a relationship assertion, linked to P's father.
The census gives the same occupation as the voter register already linked to P.
The census gives the same street address as the voter register already linked to P ('530 Baldwin, Niles, Ohio').
No namesake of P is recorded, so nothing caps the link.
The namesake recorded is of another person, not of P.
A speculative link is what the cap asks for.
An absent-basis assertion records that a search found nothing; it is never judged.
Two godparents share a role but each has its own record id; the second is linked to P's wife.
A marriage extracted with one record id per persona: the bride on her own record is linked to P's wife (marina-lopez).
The namesake's census: his wife, also a Mary Smith, is linked to P's wife, so the census ties to P (robert-lord X9G3-FRG).
The wife is a hand-built person with no sources, so she is not read as made from the record, and her link ties it (alvro-taylor).
A source holding two burials, the father's in 1802 and the son's in 1862, is read as one record, so the son's burial ties the father's (mikkel src_004).
P's marriage to I2 cites only this marriage, recorded after linking it; the bride's link to I2 ties it. I2 is not made from it alone, since her refs reach another record (georg 09-16, R1).
The son heads his own household and is linked to P, his father; the household's occupation matches P's own census, so the occupation ties it (R5).
